name: Communization
summary: Communization is the current of post-1968 French ultra-left communism, developed by Théorie Communiste, Troploin and Endnotes, that holds the revolution must itself be the abolition of the state, exchange, wage labour, property and the division of labour, with no transitional period. It holds that the working class can no longer affirm itself as a class or take power, and must abolish itself in the process. It rejects the party, the union, workers' councils and self-management as forms of the workers' movement that has ended, and also rejects alternative communes within capitalism.
scope: The Théorie Communiste / Endnotes line of communization, with Troploin and the essays of Communization and its Discontents (2011). It excludes the Tiqqun and Invisible Committee insurrectionist usage, which Endnotes and De Mattis criticise as a different, alternativist idea, and it excludes earlier left communism. Where the texts are silent on a question outside political economy and revolutionary strategy, the answer is null.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Théorie Communiste lists abolition of the division of labour among the communist measures and ties it to rebuilding the physical separation of town and country and of workplaces.

abolish-ip.rationale: The abolition of all forms of property is a measure of communization; the sources do not discuss patents and copyright separately, so the answer follows from the general abolition and is held at medium.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Théorie Communiste names the dissolution of wage labour, of exchange and of value as measures taken in the course of the revolution.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Théorie Communiste lists dissolving wage labour among the first measures a revolution cannot do without.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The abolition of both the state and property rules out state ownership of land as a goal.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Endnotes says no individual or group can overcome the capital relation by its own actions, and that the revolution is not the sum of already-communizing acts.

class-collaboration.rationale: Endnotes says anything short of the working class's abolition leaves capital with an obliging partner, and the class relation is an antagonism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Communization is derived from the dynamics of the class struggle; the sources treat the capital-labour relation as the engine of change, though they do not state a general law of history.

clerical-rule.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here rule by senior clergy, is contrary to it.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: Staged revolution is a transitional period, which Endnotes and Théorie Communiste reject.

conscription.rationale: Conscription is an instrument of the state, which communization abolishes.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Endnotes denies any autonomy, alternative or secession within capital and calls sharing at the margins non-revolutionary; De Mattis criticises communes and cooperatives as illusory alternatives.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Noys reports TC's view that workers' states reinforced capitalism and Endnotes treats the workers' state as lost, so defending one is not a task.

democracy-best.rationale: The state form is to be abolished, and Théorie Communiste calls democratic managerial solutions an alternative that preserves the middle strata's positions.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Endnotes says a transition built on a prior victory of the working class as working class is no longer imaginable, and Noys reports that a dictatorship of the proletariat can no longer be proposed.

direct-action.rationale: Both reject reformism and treat revolution as a rupture; Théorie Communiste describes riots and blockades as the form struggle takes, and Noys places unions and parties inside capital.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Théorie Communiste describes the extension of a situation where everything is freely available, without exchange or appropriation, and treats the very notion of the product as abolished.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here authority from God, is contrary to it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here dynastic succession in a state, is contrary to it.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Théorie Communiste describes revolution as undermining and calling into doubt ethnic and racial nationality, since identities are overdeterminations of class that the revolution confronts.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gonzalez argues, as Théorie Communiste does, that gender is produced by the relations that reproduce capital and must be destroyed in the course of revolution.

gradual-change.rationale: Théorie Communiste says that from struggles over demands to revolution there can only be a rupture, a qualitative leap.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: Affirming labour against capital is the programmatist stance that Endnotes and Théorie Communiste say has ended; the goal is to abolish both poles of the relation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here scriptural law, is contrary to it.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Théorie Communiste speaks of the de-essentialization of labour and the dissolution of wage labour and the state, which a legal duty to work would perpetuate.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Exchange and the state are both to be abolished, and Noys notes socialist accumulation under party states reinforced capital, so a party-led market economy is the opposite of its aim.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Communization abolishes exchange and the value form altogether, so markets cannot be the means of allocation; Théorie Communiste lists the abolition of exchange among the measures of the revolution itself.

material-over-identity.rationale: Gonzalez argues the revolution cannot be built on a unifying workers' identity and must abolish gender and all divisions in its course.

means-match-ends.rationale: Endnotes denies that communization is prefigurative practice, while Théorie Communiste says communist measures are the production of communism; the sources point both ways.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here a hereditary monarchy, is contrary to it.

municipal-property.rationale: Communization abolishes property relations rather than moving them to the community; Endnotes notes that what is held in common is often the counterpart of an appropriation.

national-self-determination.rationale: Abolition of the state is a measure of the revolution, and Théorie Communiste rejects national alternative solutions, so a right of every nation to its own state is not one of its aims.

natural-rulers.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here rule by a naturally fitted few, is contrary to it.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Communization claims to be the communist production of communism, so a third course is rejected.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A government enforcing property is contrary to the abolition of both state and property.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: Endnotes opposes the transitional period, and Théorie Communiste says measures of communization are not a period of transition but the revolution.

one-party-rule.rationale: Endnotes rejects the Leninist model and the workers' state, and Noys says the revolutions of programmatism reinforced capitalism.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Noys notes TC treats unions, parties and social reforms as internal forms of capital, and the state must be abolished, not captured.

party-commands-army.rationale: Rule by a party-state is rejected along with the state form.

party-controls-media.rationale: Rule by a party-state is rejected along with the state form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gonzalez says that within a world defined by productive labour women are always less than men, and the workers' movement kept women in their place.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Théorie Communiste rejects national alternative solutions and the national delimitation of accumulation that underlay workers' identity.

pay-for-effort.rationale: A wage scaled to effort presupposes the wage relation, which Théorie Communiste lists for dissolution.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here rule by personal oaths, is contrary to it.

production-for-use.rationale: The abolition of value and of production for capital is the central content of communization, with activity no longer organised around products to be exchanged.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Théorie Communiste places the exploitation of surplus-value-producing labour at the heart of the contradiction between proletariat and capital.

property-fundamental.rationale: The revolution is the abolition of all forms of property; Endnotes defines communization as the undoing of the property relations that constitute the capitalist class relation.

public-ownership.rationale: Théorie Communiste lists the abolition of the state and of all forms of property, and the scholarship on the current notes that it rejects a takeover of the means of production in favour of destroying the value form, so state ownership of industry is not its goal.

race-social-construct.rationale: Théorie Communiste says all identities, racial and ethnic ones included, are constructed, historical and fragile, though it adds that racialization is a necessary form of appearance with real effects; the sources do not discuss a scientific basis for race.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Théorie Communiste warns against entrepreneurs of racialization yet says identities can serve as points of support and that racialized proletarians struggle against their racialization; the text points both ways.

reification.rationale: Théorie Communiste states that relations between individuals are fixed in things because exchange value is by nature material.

restore-past-order.rationale: Williams rejects the thought of return to a lost commons or a pre-capitalist community as a basis for communism.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here a sacred head of state, is contrary to it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Endnotes holds that the social forms reproducing the capital relation, the state among them, cannot serve as instruments of revolution, and Théorie Communiste describes confronting and dismantling the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Endnotes calls it delusional to conceive revolution in terms of workers' power, since the class must abolish itself.

socialized-markets.rationale: Communization abolishes exchange and value, not merely their legal owners; a market with worker or public owners keeps both, and De Mattis shows cooperatives remain inside capital's circuits.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here an unbound ruler, is contrary to it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Noys summarises Théorie Communiste as holding that programmatist revolutions, with socialist accumulation and the workers' state, reinforced capitalism; the exact label state capitalism is not quoted, so medium.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: State finance for worker enterprises combines the state form and workers' management, both of which these sources reject as non-revolutionary.

state-harmful.rationale: Théorie Communiste lists the abolition of the state among the measures of revolution, and Endnotes counts the state form among the forms implicated in the reproduction of capital.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The state must be abolished, with no transitional period.

strong-leader.rationale: The state is to be abolished as a form implicated in the reproduction of capital, so a doctrine of legitimate authority over society, here a strong leader above gridlock, is contrary to it.

total-state.rationale: A state directing all life is the opposite of the abolition of the state that these sources require.

unions-good.rationale: Noys's summary of Théorie Communiste places trade unions among the institutions through which workers' struggle became internal to capital under programmatism, and Endnotes says such social forms will not be instruments of the revolution.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Noys's account of programmatism treats unions as institutions internal to capital, and Endnotes rejects management of production by and for workers as a route.

vanguard-party.rationale: Endnotes rejects Leninist conceptions and Noys notes communization drops the party form, and Théorie Communiste has no revolutionary agent apart from the proletariat's own self-transformation; De Mattis distinguishes it from an avant-garde.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Gonzalez says gender is constitutive of capital's central contradiction and cannot be reconciled with the working class and capital existing together; it is overcome only by communization.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Noys reports Théorie Communiste's critique of the programmatist theology of labour, and TC itself describes the proletariat's task as the de-essentialization of labour.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Théorie Communiste says communization supersedes the dilemma between Leninist or democratic class alliances and the proletariat alone, both described as defeats.

worker-ownership.rationale: Théorie Communiste and Endnotes reject self-management and workers' management of existing means of production as a form of the working class affirming itself; De Mattis adds that a workers' cooperative still self-exploits through the circuits of capital.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: Théorie Communiste rejects democratic class alliances and national managerial solutions preserving the middle strata.

workers-councils.rationale: Endnotes treats councilist and Leninist conceptions of revolution as utopian today, and Théorie Communiste says self-organisation is not the revolutionary perspective.

workers-nation.rationale: Théorie Communiste speaks of a global working class and rejects national alternative solutions.

workers-own-party.rationale: The workers' party belongs to programmatism, whose end Endnotes and Théorie Communiste announce.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: Programmatist parties campaigning for reforms are part of the cycle Endnotes and Théorie Communiste declare finished; reformism is described as impossible.

missingStatements.text: A communist revolution is the working class abolishing itself.
missingStatements.rationale: Endnotes and Théorie Communiste both define the revolution as the proletariat's self-abolition, which no statement in the bank captures.

quotes.text: such an overcoming must necessarily be the direct self-abolition of the working class
quotes.where: Endnotes, What are we to do?, printed p.26

quotes.text: The unity of the proletariat can only be the activity in which it abolishes itself in abolishing everything that divides it.
quotes.where: Théorie Communiste, Communization in the Present Tense, printed p.46

missingStatements.declined: Theory wording a general reader would need explained.

notes: Searched the anthology's essays for unions, democracy, parliament, party, nation, ecology, technology, gender, commons, violence and welfare. The sources cover political economy, the state, revolutionary strategy and gender; they say little on culture, ecology, technology, religion, foreign policy or liberty questions, which are null. Those answers are not inferred from the general abolition of the state and property.
